text.name: Get started with Codex + Figma
Tebra design system · A visual setup guide for designers
Follow 1–7 in reading order. Each step has instructions, a reference image and a checkpoint. Reference images show official examples or guide excerpts, not a completed Tebra setup.
Open the full setup guide ↗
1 Download the repository
Bring the building rules onto your computer.
Official GitHub screenshot. The sample repo shown is not Tebra; use the URL in the instructions.
Image source ↗
DO THIS

In GitHub Desktop, sign into the account with repository access. Choose File → Clone Repository → URL. Paste the design-system URL below. Choose a local Code folder and click Clone. Keep one working copy. Reuse an existing checkout instead of cloning again.
Repository: danielcole-tebra/design-system For source checks, clone kareo-engineering/web-app-v2 beside it when access is available.
Open the Tebra repository ↗
CHECKPOINT
You can open the local design-system folder and see AGENTS.md, LIBRARY.md, COMPOSITIONS.md and OPEN-ISSUES.md.
2 Open a local Codex project
Make the repository the context for your design work.
Browser capture of OpenAI’s project-view illustration. It is not a screenshot of a participant’s setup.
Image source ↗
DO THIS

In Codex, create a local project named Tebra design system. Open Edit project → Add folder and select the cloned design-system folder. Make it the primary folder. Attach web-app-v2 too if you cloned it. Start a new chat in this project.
Ask Codex to read AGENTS.md, confirm the path and branch, check Git and Node.js, and run the read-only LIBRARY.md index helper.
Exact first-message prompt ↗
CHECKPOINT
Codex reads the real local files. Git, Node.js and the helper work. Missing source-code access is reported.
3 Connect Figma to Codex
Give the agent the tools and skills to work on the canvas.
Official Figma screenshot of the Codex plugin browser. Interface labels can vary by version.
Image source ↗
DO THIS
Open Plugins in Codex and find Figma. Choose Install Figma. Sign into your work Figma account and complete Allow access. Return to Codex. Start a new project chat if the tools have not appeared.
Ask which Figma skills and tools are available: inspect files, edit nodes, import library assets and capture screenshots.
Figma’s installation steps ↗
CHECKPOINT
The connection uses the intended work account and exposes canvas-editing capabilities. Tool availability alone is not a successful build.
4 Create your own Figma file
Give your first rebuild a clear destination.
Official Figma reference showing the Design file action. Your team folder and account will differ.
Image source ↗
DO THIS

In Figma, create a new Design file in your team’s practice location. Name it Tebra first rebuild · Your name. Create a page named First rebuild. Share the file with Daniel for review and copy the file link.
The destination is your new Design file. Keep the published Design System Rebuild library as the source of components.
Create a Figma Design file ↗
CHECKPOINT
You can edit your named file, Daniel can review it, and you have its file link for Codex.
5 Add the rebuild library
Enable Tebra components, styles and variables in your file.
Official Figma screenshot uses the sample Habitz library. Choose Design System Rebuild for this exercise.
Image source ↗
DO THIS

In your new file, open Assets → Libraries. Find Design System Rebuild and confirm its source using the link below. Choose Add to file, or leave it enabled if your team already added it. Check that you can browse Button and Text field assets.
If missing, check the signed-in account, source-file access and publication with Daniel. Do not substitute the deprecated Tebra Working UI Kit.
Open the exact Tebra source library ↗
CHECKPOINT
The correct published library is available in your destination. Opening or duplicating the library is not the same as enabling it.
6 Check the setup before building
Resolve missing access before asking for a full composition.
Screenshot of the guide’s setup-prompt excerpt. This is not a Codex response or proof of a completed setup.
Image source ↗
DO THIS

Paste the setup-check prompt into your project chat. Include your destination file link and the exact source library link. Ask for a read-only check of file identities, library discovery and available capabilities. Read the missing-setup report before continuing.
Actual imports, font loading, editability and screenshot delivery must still be verified during the first build.
Copy the full setup-check prompt ↗
CHECKPOINT
Codex reports specific findings and unknowns. A list of available tools is not treated as proof that every operation succeeded.
7 Bring in the practice card
Pending starter asset. Setup can finish before the exercise is ready.
Captured frame from Figma’s official selection-link illustration. It is not the Tebra practice card.
Image source ↗
DO THIS

Once the starter is supplied, copy its editable layers into your First rebuild page. Label it Original · Practice card and keep it intact. Select the card, then copy a link to the selection. Use that node link as Starter card and your file link as Destination.
The manual contact-details starter and verified Empty/Filled reference are not created yet. Do not substitute the old patient-search benchmark.
Open the first-rebuild exercise ↗
CHECKPOINT
When the asset is ready, your editable starter and its selection link identify the same card. Preserve it beside the rebuilt states.
Before your first rebuild
A quick readiness check, plus what happens next.
ACCOUNTS + TOOLS
Work account in Codex GitHub repository access Git and Node.js available Work Figma account Published rebuild library access Akkurat LL available to the Figma service
YOUR WORKSPACE

Local design-system folder is primary Your own editable Design file Rebuild library added to that file Daniel has access for review Starter card copied once supplied Destination and selection links ready
WHAT YOU WILL RECEIVE

An editable contact-details rebuild in Empty and Filled states. Screenshots in chat. A Figma link. A checked list of verified changes covering auto layout, library instances, typography, tokens, resizing, content and preserved originals.
PILOT NOTES

The starter asset is pending. Daniel reviews before the next build batch. Evidence must be recorded and pushed; clone access alone does not establish push access. Missing access and unverified checks stay explicit.
Full setup guide ↗
First rebuild + what-changed checklist ↗
